title: Foundations: Thrash Metal - The Complete Guide
summary: What Thrash Metal is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Thrash Metal songs: Thrash metal is speed as ideology: 200-bpm downpicking, shouted vocals, and songs about war, madness, and moshing. The Big Four — Metallica, Slayer, Megadeth, Anthrax — ruled the 1980s underground.

History: Metallica's Kill 'Em All (1983) and Slayer's Reign in Blood (1986, 29 minutes of fury) defined thrash: punk speed plus metal precision, made by Bay Area teenagers.

How the songs work: Thrash Metal favors the keys of E, Eb, D. Common forms include Blistering verse-chorus with extended solo trade-offs; Tempo changes: fast, faster, breakdown. Players should master downpicking at 200+ bpm first, then the mosh breakdown: half-time slam riff. Speed needs open strings; no capos.

title: Master of Puppets - Thrash Metal Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Master of Puppets by Metallica (1986).
body:
Master of Puppets — Metallica, 1986. Eight minutes of thrash perfection.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of D):
D5 | D#5 | E5 | F5

This study chart uses the 'Chromatic menace' progression, the Thrash Metal workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: blistering verse-chorus with extended solo trade-offs. Listen for shouted gang choruses — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Thrash Metal pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let shouted gang choruses. Speed needs open strings; no capos. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
